# DOMAIN.md: recipe index (generated; do not edit)

Each recipe is a full domain blueprint the build tool reads later. Use this index only to: map journey steps to recipes (stage 4), and ask the recipe decisions that change what users or the owner experience or risk (stage 5). Leave purely technical decisions to the build.

  - Un-tagged endpoint policy · options: allow (migration) / deny · default: deny — fail closed (I1)
  - Deleting a role in use · options: refuse / reassign-to-default · default: refuse
  - Credential type · options: password-only / api-keys / both · default: match what the app already has — never add a login…

### booking  (risk high; pairs with [auth-roles, payments, monitor])
- What you get: your customers reserve your scarce thing — a seat, a room, a staff member's hour, a table, a unit of stock — and the system NEVER gives the same slot to two people, even when two people click at the exact same second.
- Provides: POST create-reservation (public) | GET availability (public) | GET reservation-by-code (public, no PII) | staff list/reschedule/cancel endpoints | events: booking.created, booking.cancelled
- Decisions:
  - Buffer time between reservations · options: none / fixed N min / per-service · default: none (back-to-back legal via half-open intervals)
  - Overbooking policy · options: never / allow N / waitlist · default: never — the whole point of I1
  - Cancellation window · options: free-until-X / always-free / non-refundable · default: always-free (this workbook takes no money — the payments…
  - Grid size · options: 5 / 15 / 30 / 60 min · default: 15 min
  - Who creates reservations · options: public / staff-only · default: public
- Gotchas: Modeling duration/price on the reservation instead of the service · One giant `bookings` table with a text "resource" column · Treating availability as free-text hours · Hard-deleting a cancelled reservation · No `code` handle, exposing the numeric id · Mixing storage of local and UTC times
